SUBJECT:       DUANE ARNOLD ENERGY CENTER – NRC INSPECTION REPORT
               05000331/2026003 AND 07200032/2026001

Dear Ray Wheaton:

On September 22, 2026, the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) completed an
inspection at the Duane Arnold Energy Center in Palo, Iowa. On September 22, 2026, the NRC
inspectors discussed the results of this inspection with Dave Sluszka and other members of
your staff. The results of the inspection are documented in the enclosed report.

No findings or violations of more-than-Minor significance were identified during this inspection.

This letter, its enclosure, and your response (if any) will be made available for public inspection
and copying at http://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/adams.html and at the NRC Public Document
Room in accordance with Title 10 of the Code of Federal Regulations 2.390, “Public
Inspections, Exemptions, Requests for Withholding.”

                                              Sincerely,



                                                              Signed by David Hills on 10/06/26

                                              David E. Hills, Chief
                                              Spent Fuel Storage Oversight Branch
                                              Div of Fuel Cycle & Mtrls Oversight

                                           SUMMARY

The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) continued monitoring the licensee’s
performance by conducting an NRC inspection at Duane Arnold Energy Center, in accordance
with IMC 2690, “Inspection Program for Storage of Spent Reactor Fuel and Reactor-Related
Greater-Than-Class C Waste at Independent Spent Fuel Storage Installations and for 10 CFR
Part 71 Transportation Packagings.” This is the NRC’s program for overseeing the safe
operation of licensed independent spent fuel storage installations (ISFSIs). Refer to
https://www.nrc.gov/waste/spent-fuel-storage for more information.

                                List of Findings and Violations

No violations of more-than-Minor significance were identified.

                                  Additional Tracking Items

None.




                                                2
 SITE STATUS

The Duane Arnold Energy Center (DAEC) ceased power operations and subsequently removed
all fuel from the reactor, as certified in a letter to the NRC on October 12, 2020. On January 23,
2025, NextEra submitted a letter to the NRC requesting exemptions from certain portions of the
requirements of 10 CFR 50.82(a)(2) to pursue the potential reauthorization of power operations.

INSPECTION SCOPES

Inspections were conducted using the appropriate portions of the inspection procedures (IPs) in
effect at the beginning of the inspection unless otherwise noted. Currently approved IPs with
their attached revision histories are located on the public website at http://www.nrc.gov/reading-
rm/doc-collections/insp-manual/inspection-procedure/index.html. Inspections are declared
completed when the IP requirements most appropriate to the inspection activity were met
consistent with Inspection Manual Chapter 2690, “Inspection Program for Storage of Spent
Reactor Fuel and Reactor-Related Greater-than-Class C Waste at Independent Spent Fuel
Storage Installations and for 10 CFR Part 71 Transportation Packagings.” The inspectors
reviewed selected procedures and records, observed activities, and interviewed personnel to
assess licensee performance and compliance with Commission rules and regulations, license
conditions, site procedures, and standards.


60855 - Operation of an Independent Spent Fuel Storage Installation

The inspectors verified that the operations of the ISFSI are performed in compliance with the
applicable regulatory requirements.

Operation of an Independent Spent Fuel Storage Installation (1 Sample)

(1)   The inspectors reviewed applicable portions of the licensing and design bases
      including: (1) the final safety analysis report; (2) the technical specifications (TS); and
      the certificate of compliance (CoC). The inspectors reviewed a sample of operating
      procedures, overall ISFSI monitoring (including condition reports and program
      changes), and associated ISFSI program effectiveness. The inspectors evaluated
      activities related to long-term operation and ISFSI monitoring and performed visual
      inspections of the ISFSI to identify potential hazards and/or signs of degradation.

      The inspectors evaluated and reviewed the following from September 14 through
      September 18, 2026:
         • Walkdown of the ISFSI pad
         • Emergency Exercise
         • ISFSI monitoring activities were performed in accordance with approved
             procedures
         • Quality Assurance in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements
         • Corrective action program

      The inspectors evaluated the following change reviews:
         • 72.48 Screening for EC299127
         • 72.48 Screening for EC299128



                                                 3
 60859 - Independent Spent Fuel Storage Installation (ISFSI) License Renewal Inspection

The inspectors verified the site's ISFSI renewal program effectively implements aging
management programs (AMPs) and activities relating to the renewal of an ISFSI. Inspectors
assessed the licensee's programs that ensure dry cask storage systems and related structures,
systems, and components (SSCs) will safely perform their intended functions during the period
of extended operations (PEO).

Independent Spent Fuel Storage Installation (ISFSI) License Renewal Inspection (1 Sample)

(1)    The 20-year original Standardized NUHOMS® Horizontal Modular Storage
       System license period ended January 23, 2015. On December 11, 2017, TN
       Americas LLC received a 40-year license renewal for the Standardized NUHOMS®
       Horizontal Modular Storage System from the NRC.

       The inspectors reviewed applicable portions of the licensing and design bases
       including: (1) the final safety analysis report; (2) the technical specifications (TS); and
       (3) Certificate of Compliance (CoC) 1004. The inspectors verified that the ISFSI
       license renewal program including aging management programs (AMPs), time limited
       aging analyses (TLAAs), and regulatory commitments were implemented for
       structures, systems, and components (SSCs) by reviewing the following activities.

       The inspectors observed and evaluated the following activities from September 14
       through September 18, 2026:
           • Visual inspections of the ISFSI to identify potential hazards and/or signs of
              degradation
           • Collection and use of aging management operating experience
           • Scoping, planning, and subsequent implementation of ISFSI AMPs for the
              various SSCs which require an AMP per licensing requirements
           • Administrative controls for aging management
           • Quality Assurance Program (QAP) implementation of aging management
              activities
           • Tollgate assessment
           • Sampled conditions in the renewed license/CoC and technical specifications
           • All applicable TLAAs were reviewed including, but not limited to: Dry Shielded
              Canister (DSC) Fatigue Evaluation, Transfer Cask Fatigue Evaluation, DSC
              Poison Plates Boron Depletion Evaluation, and Thermal Performance of
              Horizontal Storage Modules (HSMs) for the PEO, as described in the NRC
              safety evaluation report and FSAR
           • Assessment of the licensee's acceptance criteria for age-related degradation
              within the AMPs
           • Assessment of the corrective action program for age-related degradation
              within the AMPs



INSPECTION RESULTS

No violations of more-than-Minor significance were identified.




                                                 4
 EXIT MEETINGS AND DEBRIEFS

The inspectors verified no proprietary information was retained or documented in this report.

   •   On September 22, 2026, the inspectors presented the NRC inspection results to Dave
       Sluszka, Vice President of Long-Range Execution, and other members of the licensee
       staff.
